column2: Invite Griqualand West into the Republic

The victory over Britain has opened a debate about the republic's remaining frontiers. Send a delegation to Griqualand West demanding incorporation under a common administration. Its council may accept articles of union or defend its separate government. An accepted agreement will transfer its territory and require a settlement of public obligations and local institutions. A refusal returns the question to the Volksraad, which can preserve peace or order a campaign. Negotiations can begin with an independent government or our own protectorate, while a foreign dependency requires its relationship with its overlord to be resolved first.
A Delegation from the Republic

The diamond fields and the communities of Griqualand West lie at the meeting point of competing land titles, trading routes and political loyalties. A common government promises more orderly customs and protection for commerce, but the Griqua council fears that its voice and existing land rights will disappear beneath the weight of a larger republic. Republican delegates now place articles of incorporation before the council. Acceptance would transfer foreign affairs, public obligations and territorial administration to the common government. Refusal preserves the council's position, but may lead the Volksraad to demand by force what it cannot obtain through negotiation.
Griqualand West Accepts the Articles of Union

The diamond fields and the communities of Griqualand West lie at the meeting point of competing land titles, trading routes and political loyalties. A common government promises more orderly customs and protection for commerce, but the Griqua council fears that its voice and existing land rights will disappear beneath the weight of a larger republic. The council has accepted incorporation, and commissioners will now prepare the handover of public records and offices. Agreement on sovereignty does not settle every question of government. The Volksraad must choose whether local councils will retain substantial responsibility or whether the districts will enter a common administrative system. The treaty offers a beginning, but its durability will depend on how the republic treats the communities whose territory and obligations it now assumes.
Griqualand West Rejects Incorporation

The diamond fields and the communities of Griqualand West lie at the meeting point of competing land titles, trading routes and political loyalties. A common government promises more orderly customs and protection for commerce, but the Griqua council fears that its voice and existing land rights will disappear beneath the weight of a larger republic. The delegates return without signatures. The council refuses to surrender its separate administration merely because the republic has defeated Britain. The Volksraad must now decide whether to preserve the peace or send the commandants to enforce incorporation. A campaign would seek the remaining territory of the opposing government, and bring responsibility for the institutions and communities within it. Victory cannot relieve the republic of the cost of administering what it conquers.
Griqualand West and the Common Republic

The diamond fields and the communities of Griqualand West lie at the meeting point of competing land titles, trading routes and political loyalties. A common government promises more orderly customs and protection for commerce, but the Griqua council fears that its voice and existing land rights will disappear beneath the weight of a larger republic. The question of sovereignty has now been decided, and the district commissioners ask for instructions. The republic can recognise local councils and adapt existing records to the new government, or finance a common administration of courts, taxation and public works. Both courses require the settlement of obligations and a clear place for the districts in republican institutions. The peace will be judged through the daily work of officials and the security of households, rather than through the ceremony of annexation alone.

Commemorate the War and Support Its Veterans

Peace has returned, but the commando rolls contain names that will not answer another summons. Endow district memorials and a fund for wounded veterans and bereaved households. A public act of remembrance can bind the districts to the republic while acknowledging obligations that victory alone cannot discharge. Local councils will record the fallen and administer relief under the scrutiny of the Volksraad.
